title: Own the data you change
summary: A service should clearly own the data it changes. Other services use its interface rather than editing its tables directly.
introduction: A service should clearly own the data it changes. Other services use its interface rather than editing its tables directly. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain own the data you change
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A service should clearly own the data it changes. Other services use its interface rather than editing its tables directly.

blocks.code:
Catalog owns Book records
Loans owns Loan records
Loans asks Catalog whether book 17 exists
blocks.title: Own the data you change

blocks.text: Catalog remains responsible for book facts. Loans stays responsible for lending facts.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Decide which service changes a book title.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Shared writable tables create hidden links between services.
For more detail later, use this [Microservices further reading](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/microservices/).

seo.title: Microservices: Own the data you change
seo.description: Learn about own the data you change in Microservices. Follow a small example, understand the result, and practise with a clear question.
